parts.name: Common tendon of origin: semitendinosus + biceps femoris long head

parts.name: Semimembranosus origin tendon (lateral to the conjoint tendon)

parts.name: Long head: lateral aponeurosis

parts.name: Proximal MTJ zone of the long head (and its free proximal tendon)
parts.description: Sprint-type first-time hamstring strains were all in the long head of biceps femoris; involvement of the proximal free tendon and proximity to the ischial tuberosity predicted longer recovery. Of 15 athletes, 5 injuries were at the proximal MTJ, 2 at the distal MTJ; all intramuscular injuries lay at the MTJ within the muscle.

anchor.note: free proximal tendon from the ischial tuberosity; MTJ typically about 10 cm from the origin (Miller 2007: ST and BF muscle bellies separate at 9.9 +/- 1.5 cm)

parts.citation: Askling CM et al. 2007 Am J Sports Med 35(2):197-206 doi:10.1177/0363546506294679 PMID:17170160; De Smet AA et al. 2000 AJR Am J Roentgenol 174(2):393-399 doi:10.2214/ajr.174.2.1740393 PMID:10658712

parts.name: Proximal MTJ (common tendon splits from biceps femoris long head)

parts.name: Insertion complex on the greater trochanter (lateral + superoposterior facets together)

parts.name: Origin: external ilium between the anterior and inferior gluteal lines, plus the sciatic notch from the inside
parts.description: Also protects the superior gluteal nerve and artery at the notch.

parts.name: Insertion: anterior facet of the greater trochanter
parts.description: Attaches to the anterior facet; the subgluteus minimus bursa lies under the tendon.

parts.name: Psoas major tendon (most medial)
parts.description: Consistently the most medial tendinous structure.

parts.name: Primary iliacus tendon
parts.description: Lies immediately lateral to the psoas major tendon within the belly of iliacus.

parts.name: Accessory iliacus tendon
parts.description: When present, lateral to the primary iliacus tendon; triple-banded in 7.5 %.

parts.name: Iliofemoral ligament: superior band

parts.name: Iliofemoral ligament: inferior band
parts.description: Restrictive in extension. Z-Anatomy 'descending part' assumed to correspond.

parts.description: In all 15 cadavers the ITB was anchored to the distal femur by fibrous strands with a layer of richly innervated fat; it is a part of the fascia lata.

parts.name: Sartorius tendon (superficial layer)
parts.description: Inserts in the superficial layer of the pes on the medial tibial surface.
parts.citation: Lee JH et al. 2014 Anat Cell Biol 47(2):127-131 doi:10.5115/acb.2014.47.2.127 PMID:24987549; Olewnik L et al. 2018 Knee Surg Sports Traumatol Arthrosc 27(9):2984-2993 doi:10.1007/s00167-018-5318-3 PMID:30535546

parts.description: The medial group of fibres from the medial head forms the posterior layer; the lateral part of the medial head forms the lateral border.

parts.name: Fibres of soleus: anteromedial part

parts.name: Plantaris tendon insertion variants relative to the Achilles tendon
parts.description: Plantaris present in 89.65 % of 58 limbs; no splitting in 63.79 %; bifurcation 19.23 % of present; trifurcation 7.69 %; four slips in one; blended with the Achilles tendon in 22.4 %.

parts.name: Medial head
parts.description: Fascicles of the medial head form the posterior layer of the Achilles tendon; the medial head is the most commonly ruptured part in tennis leg (66.7 % of 141).

parts.name: Lateral head

parts.name: Medial head distal MTJ / aponeurosis interface with soleus
parts.description: Tennis leg: rupture of the medial gastrocnemius (66.7 %) or fluid between the aponeuroses of medial gastrocnemius and soleus without rupture (21.3 %).
parts.citation: Delgado GJ et al. 2002 Radiology 224(1):112-119 doi:10.1148/radiol.2241011067 PMID:12091669

parts.name: Plantar fascia - Achilles paratenon relationship
parts.description: The plantar fascia is joined to the Achilles paratenon (through the heel periosteum) more than to the tendon itself; extends medially and laterally into the deep fasciae of abductor hallucis and abductor digiti minimi; thickness 2.09 vs 3.43 mm without / with Achilles degeneration on MRI.

parts.name: Tendinous intersection 1 (most proximal)
parts.description: Transverse fibrous band; adherent to the anterior rectus sheath.
parts.note: Position along the muscle: textbook levels (xiphoid, umbilicus, between) are NOT in the cited abstracts -> no geometry.
parts.citation: Broyles JM et al. 2018 Ann Plast Surg 80(1):50-53 doi:10.1097/SAP.0000000000001193 PMID:28671887; Anita et al. 2015 J Clin Diagn Res 9(6):AC10-AC12 doi:10.7860/JCDR/2015/14027.6028 PMID:26266107

parts.name: Tendinous intersection 2
parts.description: As intersection 1.

parts.name: Tendinous intersection 3 (most distal; marks the arcuate line)
parts.description: The arcuate line lies at the most distal intersection (80 subjects; arcuate line present in 80.4 %, 93 % of men; more than a third of women lacked it).
parts.citation: Mwachaka PM et al. 2010 Locating the arcuate line of Douglas: is it of surgical relevance? Clin Anat 23(1):84-86 doi:10.1002/ca.20877 PMID:19918879; Broyles JM et al. 2018 Ann Plast Surg 80(1):50-53 doi:10.1097/SAP.0000000000001193 PMID:28671887

parts.name: Accessory (4th) tendinous intersection
parts.description: Present in 2 of 32 cadavers (Broyles) and 1 of 54 (Anita); a 5th in 1 of 54.
parts.citation: Broyles JM et al. 2018 Ann Plast Surg 80(1):50-53 doi:10.1097/SAP.0000000000001193 PMID:28671887; Anita et al. 2015 J Clin Diagn Res 9(6):AC10-AC12 doi:10.7860/JCDR/2015/14027.6028 PMID:26266107

parts.name: Full-thickness intersections (anterior to posterior rectus sheath)
parts.description: Most intersections are incomplete (anterior sheath only); 18 % of 168 were full thickness with no intervening muscle or neurovascular structure; 42 % of hemi-abdomens had at least one.
parts.citation: Broyles JM et al. 2018 Ann Plast Surg 80(1):50-53 doi:10.1097/SAP.0000000000001193 PMID:28671887

parts.name: Anterior rectus sheath (ventral lamina)
parts.description: Essentially oblique collagen fibril bundles that intermingle; firmly adherent to the tendinous intersections.

parts.name: Posterior rectus sheath (dorsal lamina)
parts.description: Chiefly transverse fibril bundles; ends at the arcuate line (absent below it).
parts.citation: Axer H et al. 2001 J Surg Res 96(1):127-134 doi:10.1006/jsre.2000.6070 PMID:11181006; Mwachaka PM et al. 2010 Locating the arcuate line of Douglas: is it of surgical relevance? Clin Anat 23(1):84-86 doi:10.1002/ca.20877 PMID:19918879

parts.name: Arcuate line (of Douglas): lower edge of the posterior sheath
parts.description: Present in 80.4 % of 80 subjects, as a single bilateral arcade at the most distal intersection, in the upper half of the umbilicus-to-pubic-symphysis line in most; absent in more than a third of women.
parts.citation: Mwachaka PM et al. 2010 Locating the arcuate line of Douglas: is it of surgical relevance? Clin Anat 23(1):84-86 doi:10.1002/ca.20877 PMID:19918879

parts.name: Linea alba: supra-umbilical part
parts.description: Three laminae from ventral to dorsal: lamina fibrae obliquae, lamina fibrae transversae, small inconstant lamina fibrae irregularium. Diastasis threshold above the umbilicus: 10 mm (<45 y) / 15 mm (>45 y).
parts.citation: Axer H et al. 2001 J Surg Res 96(1):127-134 doi:10.1006/jsre.2000.6070 PMID:11181006; Rath AM et al. 1996 Surg Radiol Anat 18(4):281-288 doi:10.1007/BF01627606 PMID:8983107

parts.name: Linea alba: umbilical part
parts.description: Diastasis recti is defined by an inter-rectus separation above 27 mm at the umbilical ring (both age groups; Rath 1996).
parts.citation: Axer H et al. 2001 J Surg Res 96(1):127-134 doi:10.1006/jsre.2000.6070 PMID:11181006; Rath AM et al. 1996 Surg Radiol Anat 18(4):281-288 doi:10.1007/BF01627606 PMID:8983107

parts.name: Linea alba: transition zone
parts.description: Region between umbilical and infra-arcuate parts.

parts.name: Linea alba: infra-arcuate part
parts.description: Below the arcuate line (no posterior sheath). Diastasis threshold below the umbilicus: 9 mm (<45 y) / 14 mm (>45 y).
parts.citation: Axer H et al. 2001 J Surg Res 96(1):127-134 doi:10.1006/jsre.2000.6070 PMID:11181006; Rath AM et al. 1996 Surg Radiol Anat 18(4):281-288 doi:10.1007/BF01627606 PMID:8983107

parts.name: Puboperineal part
parts.description: Pubic origin to the perineal body. Part names from Kearney 2004; the descriptions beyond the part name are not all in the abstract.
parts.evidence: literature review (265 studies, 9 qualifying) of origin-insertion pairs

parts.name: Pubovaginal part (female)
parts.description: Pubic origin to the vaginal wall. Part names from Kearney 2004; the descriptions beyond the part name are not all in the abstract.
parts.evidence: literature review (265 studies, 9 qualifying) of origin-insertion pairs

parts.name: Puboanal part
parts.description: Pubic origin to the anus / intersphincteric groove. Z-Anatomy carries the 'pubo-analis muscle' as a separate mesh. Part names from Kearney 2004; the descriptions beyond the part name are not all in the abstract.
parts.evidence: literature review (265 studies, 9 qualifying) of origin-insertion pairs

parts.name: Puborectal part (puborectalis)
parts.description: Forms the sling behind the anorectal junction; the upper outer half of the sphincter in Stoker's account. Part names from Kearney 2004; the descriptions beyond the part name are not all in the abstract.
parts.evidence: literature review (265 studies, 9 qualifying) of origin-insertion pairs
parts.citation: Kearney R et al. 2004 Obstet Gynecol 104(1):168-173 doi:10.1097/01.AOG.0000128906.61529.6b PMID:15229017; Stoker J et al. 2009 Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol 23(4):463-475 doi:10.1016/j.bpg.2009.04.008 PMID:19647683

parts.name: Iliococcygeal part
parts.description: From the tendinous arch to the anococcygeal raphe / coccyx. Part names from Kearney 2004; the descriptions beyond the part name are not all in the abstract.
parts.evidence: literature review (265 studies, 9 qualifying) of origin-insertion pairs

parts.name: Classic subcutaneous / superficial / deep subdivision (NOT confirmed)
parts.description: Histology-guided dissection (fetal, newborn, adult pelves) did not confirm the classical tripartite subdivision; the external sphincter turns into the internal sphincter and encloses the longitudinal muscle bundles; it is not a complete circle in some planes.
parts.citation: Fritsch H et al. 2002 Dis Colon Rectum 45(2):188-194 doi:10.1007/s10350-004-6144-x PMID:11852331

parts.name: Outer striated layer: external sphincter (lower outer half) + puborectalis (upper outer half)
parts.description: The anal sphincter is multilayered: smooth-muscle internal sphincter inside, outer striated layer made of the external sphincter below and puborectalis above; the external sphincter is continuous with the rectum at the anorectal junction.
parts.citation: Stoker J et al. 2009 Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol 23(4):463-475 doi:10.1016/j.bpg.2009.04.008 PMID:19647683

parts.name: Lateral ligament of the rectum: medial part (rectal branches of the pelvic plexus)
parts.description: Lateral ligament divides into a lateral and a medial part by its relation to the pelvic plexus; the medial part consists of rectal branches of the pelvic plexus with connective tissue.

passes.traversing_text: rectal branches of the pelvic (inferior hypogastric) plexus
passes.through: lateral ligament of the rectum (endopelvic fascia)

parts.citation: Sato K et al. 1991 Surg Radiol Anat 13(1):17-22 doi:10.1007/BF01623135 PMID:2053040

parts.name: Lateral ligament of the rectum: lateral part (superoanterior = middle rectal artery; inferoposterior = pelvic splanchnic nerves)
parts.description: The middle rectal artery was present in the lateral ligament in only 22.2 % (18/81); the inferoposterior subdivision contains the pelvic splanchnic nerves. Church 1987: the middle rectal artery runs below the lateral ligaments on levator ani; accessory middle rectal artery in 25 %.
parts.variability: MRA in ligament 22.2 % (Sato) vs not in ligament (Church)

passes.traversing_text: middle rectal artery (variable), pelvic splanchnic nerves

parts.note: Two sources disagree on whether the middle rectal artery is inside the ligament: recorded as a conflict, not resolved.
parts.citation: Sato K et al. 1991 Surg Radiol Anat 13(1):17-22 doi:10.1007/BF01623135 PMID:2053040; Church JM et al. 1987 Int J Colorectal Dis 2(3):158-166 doi:10.1007/BF01648000 PMID:3309101

parts.name: Penetration of Denonvilliers' fascia by the middle rectal artery
parts.description: According to Church 1987 the middle rectal artery reaches the rectum by penetrating Denonvilliers' fascia.
parts.citation: Church JM et al. 1987 Int J Colorectal Dis 2(3):158-166 doi:10.1007/BF01648000 PMID:3309101

parts.name: Rectosacral fascia (Waldeyer): posterior attachment of the rectum to S3-S4
parts.description: Dense connective tissue between the posterior wall of the rectum and the 3rd-4th sacral vertebrae, carrying branches of the lateral and median sacral vessels and sacral splanchnic nerves; must be incised deliberately to enter the presacral space.

passes.traversing_text: branches of lateral and median sacral vessels; sacral splanchnic nerves

parts.citation: Sato K et al. 1991 Surg Radiol Anat 13(1):17-22 doi:10.1007/BF01623135 PMID:2053040; Church JM et al. 1987 Int J Colorectal Dis 2(3):158-166 doi:10.1007/BF01648000 PMID:3309101

parts.name: Anorectal junction through the puborectalis sling
parts.description: Puborectalis forms the upper outer half of the striated outer sphincter layer at the anorectal junction (the project muscle record describes the U-shaped sling behind the junction); the external sphincter is continuous with the rectum there.
parts.note: Ambiguity: the owner's word 'ברקטום' could mean rectum or rectus; both are covered (rectum here, rectus abdominis + rectus sheath above).
parts.citation: Stoker J et al. 2009 Best Pract Res Clin Gastroenterol 23(4):463-475 doi:10.1016/j.bpg.2009.04.008 PMID:19647683; Kearney R et al. 2004 Obstet Gynecol 104(1):168-173 doi:10.1097/01.AOG.0000128906.61529.6b PMID:15229017

parts.name: Pudendal canal (Alcock): pudendal nerve and vessels in a split of the obturator fascia
parts.description: Canal wall is formed by splitting of the obturator fascia (and not of the lunate fascia); mean length 1.6 cm in adults; contains the pudendal nerve and vessels; branches arise inside it in nearly all.
parts.citation: Shafik A et al. 1999 Am Surg 65(2):176-180 PMID:9926755; Robert R et al. 1998 Surg Radiol Anat 20(2):93-98 doi:10.1007/BF01628908 PMID:9658526

parts.name: Pudendal nerve conflict sites: sacrotuberous-sacrospinous gap, Alcock canal, falciform process
parts.description: Three possible conflictual settings for the pudendal nerve and its branches.

passes.through: between sacrotuberous and sacrospinous ligaments; pudendal canal; falciform process of sacrotuberous ligament

parts.citation: Robert R et al. 1998 Surg Radiol Anat 20(2):93-98 doi:10.1007/BF01628908 PMID:9658526

parts.name: Posterior layer: superficial lamina
parts.description: Dominated by the aponeuroses of latissimus dorsi and serratus posterior inferior.

parts.name: Posterior layer: deep lamina (paraspinal retinacular sheath)
parts.description: Encapsulates the paraspinal muscles; forms the lumbar interfascial triangle (LIFT) with the middle layer.

parts.name: Lateral raphe (junction with transversus abdominis aponeurosis)
parts.description: Thickened dense connective tissue marking the junction of the hypaxial (abdominal) and epaxial (paraspinal) compartments.

parts.name: Thoracolumbar composite at the lumbosacral base
parts.description: All layers fuse into a composite that attaches to the PSIS and the sacrotuberous ligament.

parts.name: Superior cluneal nerves crossing the posterior iliac crest
parts.description: Three branches (medial, intermediate, lateral) cross the iliac crest a mean 5.0, 6.5 and 7.3 cm lateral to the PSIS; middle cluneal nerves originate about at the PSIS level (2 cm above to 1.5 cm below) and traverse the paraspinal muscles to the dorsal sacrum.

passes.through: thoracolumbar fascia / gluteal fascia at the iliac crest

parts.name: PIP proper collateral ligament
parts.description: Arises widely from dorsal and proximal to the fovea on the side of the proximal phalangeal head and inserts along most of the side of the base of the middle phalanx; stout; fibres parallel to the middle phalanx in all joint positions (differs from most line drawings).
parts.evidence: microscope dissection n=8 PIP joints + 2 histology
parts.note: Z-Anatomy has one mesh per hand for ALL interphalangeal collaterals (proper + accessory not separated): the position is the pooled centroid.

parts.name: PIP accessory collateral ligament
parts.description: Less substantial; lies between the proper collateral ligament and the volar plate; suspends the plate laterally with the A3 pulley; contains the assemblage nuclei (mechanoreceptors).

parts.name: PIP volar (palmar) plate: distal fibrous portion
parts.description: Distal fibrous portion anchoring to the base of the middle phalanx.

parts.name: PIP volar plate: proximal membranous portion + check-rein ligaments
parts.description: Proximal membranous portion continuous with the bilateral check-rein ligaments; proximal attachments distinctive, distal attachments variable (Bowers).

parts.name: DIP accessory collateral ligament
parts.description: Contains the assemblage nuclei of the DIP joint; the C3 pulley contains their proximal region, the A5 pulley the middle and distal parts.
parts.citation: Chikenji T et al. 2011 J Hand Surg Am 36(3):406-412 doi:10.1016/j.jhsa.2010.11.050 PMID:21371623

parts.description: Becomes subcutaneous a mean 9.0 cm proximal to the radial styloid, passing between the tendons of brachioradialis and extensor carpi radialis longus; branches a mean 5.1 cm proximal to the styloid.

parts.description: Fibrous band ~4 mm wide from the medial epicondyle to the olecranon forming the proximal roof; absent in 1 of 27 (type 0), lax in extension and taut in flexion in 17 (type Ia).

passes.through: arcade of Struthers / medial intermuscular septum

parts.name: Superficial fibular (peroneal) nerve pierces the crural fascia
parts.description: In 85 legs the nerve or its branches passed through the crural fascia 3-18 cm proximal to the lateral malleolus; in 73 % it ran in the lateral compartment from origin to exit, 14 % crossed from the lateral to the anterior compartment, 12 % divided in two; emerges between peroneus longus and EDL at a highly variable level (sonography n=60 legs).

parts.description: 40 limbs: 552 medial perforators (mean 13.8); 52 % direct (superficial to deep), 41 % indirect muscle perforators; Cockett II/III groups 7-9 cm and 10-12 cm above the ankle; three paratibial groups 18-22, 23-27, 28-32 cm; paratibial perforators need an incision of the paratibial deep fascia.

parts.name: Segmental nerves and the deep inferior epigastric 'rectus sheath plexus' in the sheath
parts.description: The thoracolumbar nerves travel as multiple mixed segmental nerves that communicate widely in the transversus abdominis plane and in a rectus sheath plexus running with the deep inferior epigastric artery; rectus abdominis is supplied by T6-L1 with a constant L1 branch; the umbilicus always by a T10 branch.

parts.name: Umbilical ring: passage of the obliterated umbilical structures
parts.description: Round hepatic (teres) ligament, median and medial umbilical ligaments attach at/pass the umbilical ring; ring classified into five types; the umbilical fascia is a continuation of the umbilicovesicular fascia in the authors' view; hernia incidence was 25 % and all hernia cases lacked the umbilical fascia.

parts.name: Superficial head
parts.description: Prime mover of forearm pronation.

parts.name: Deep head
parts.description: Dynamic stabiliser of the distal radioulnar joint; the most distal fascicle reaches the base of the ulnar styloid; the nerves to the superficial head penetrate the deep head.

parts.name: Soleal (tendinous) arch: tibial nerve and popliteal vessels pass beneath the arch of origin of soleus
parts.description: Tibial nerve entrapment beneath the tendinous arch of origin of soleus (4 of 5 surgically confirmed cases); popliteal vein compressed by the arch in the fifth.

parts.description: The suprascapular nerve passes through the notch under the ligament, branching proximal to the notch in 15 %, at it in 54 % and distal in 31 % (93 shoulders; notch depth 5.8 mm, width 7.8 mm); the suprascapular artery normally passes above the ligament (below in 3 % of 66 limbs).
